question: True or false: zinc white, sold as a non-toxic substitute for lead white, gives a tougher, more flexible oil film?
answer: False. Zinc oxide reacts with the fatty acids of drying oil to form zinc soaps, and the film turns brittle within decades. Zinc-rich grounds and layers, common from the late 19th century, crack and flake apart. Lead white also forms soaps but ages into a tough skin. The safer white proved the weaker one.
move: A safer replacement can fail in ways the old material never did.
ask: Which safer replacement have I adopted that may fail in ways the old thing never did?
trap: Assuming the newer, safer product must also be the sturdier one.
reference: Gillian Osmond, Zinc white: a review of zinc oxide pigment properties and implications for conservation, AICCM Bulletin, 2012
